pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as three to four kettlebell sessions of 30-40 minutes plus five to fifteen minutes of daily mobility, with the rep explicitly tying it to the prospect's own injuries — 'the things that you're struggling with the most, the hamstrings, all of those things, your right shoulder, everything around that. So he's going to be able to create that plan around it for you.' Asked directly whether he had questions, the prospect said 'No, that all makes sense.' No pushback and no probing, which is notable given he had just described six to eight years of shoulder trouble and a period of training that damaged his joints.

Accepted without objection and with unusual participation — he added his own diagnosis rather than asking questions. On the fajita example he volunteered the real mechanism: 'my partner can't eat too much. She can only eat so much, so I end up eating the more to address the fact that we're not wasting anything... that is a problem that I know about that needs dealing with.' He also volunteered his own takeaway heuristic (burger with fries and water, or burger without fries and a soft drink) and accepted the correction on sugary drinks. Engaged agreement rather than passive agreement.

The pillar he selected himself when asked what would help most: 'having a set plan will definitely help. I think the community and kind of accountability aspect will definitely help because for kind of the last two years, it's always been on my own. I just work out on my own. Everything's always a solitary venture, so to speak. So I think having kind of other people who are interested and invested in my development will be a good thing.' He had already named external accountability as the missing piece before the presentation — 'if I had some outside source to say, no, no, stop changing things... having a bit of an external accountability for once, I think that that would be helpful' — and he has never had a coach of any kind.

anchors.raw: it's doable, but it's also quite a chunk of money, so I wouldn't be comfortable doing it without a sufficient level of kind of funding, because at the moment, I've only got a very little amount of savings, and I'm working on building that up... My last, kind of, 10 years have been very complicated financially, and I'm kind of at the back end of fixing that now.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor, and it is a rule rather than a preference: he will not spend against a monthly surplus without an emergency buffer behind it. £1,200 a month clear and £750 a month affordable in isolation, but he refused on principle because the reserve is not there yet. No rebuttal reaches this, which is why the rep was right to disengage.

anchors.raw: I've always done things off my own back because I feel like at the end of the day, everything that you learn... you can learn for yourself, and I like to think that I'm intelligent enough to apply things
anchors.competitor: self-directed training and Trevor's free content
anchors.note: Two and a half years of self-programming, four to six sessions a week, never missing a week, with real strength and muscle gained. He has watched most of Trevor's YouTube content and sees his reels daily. The paid offer has to beat a free method he is already executing with discipline — his own stated gap is decision fatigue, not knowledge.

anchors.raw: The economy situation in England is not great at the moment.
anchors.note: Offered as context for why the figure is out of reach, and immediately validated by the rep ('I know it's the same in a good amount of places in Western Europe'). Worth logging at scale as a recurring undercutting anchor for UK and European prospects rather than as a personal objection.

anchors.raw: It's an investment of 6k USD, which comes down to around 4.5 British.
anchors.note: The conversion made the number concrete enough for the prospect to convert it again into £750 a month unprompted, and that monthly figure is what he then judged unaffordable. Same pattern as the Frédéric call: the lump sum drew no reaction, the self-computed monthly rate did.

anchors.raw: one thing Trevor did say as well is that it does carry in, like, a business perspective, and I agree with that. If you are in good shape... or if you are in the best shape in your company, or in business meetings, that does have power. And that is something I want to work on as well.
anchors.note: He arrived pre-sold on the value argument, having absorbed it from Trevor's content, and extended it himself to cognitive performance at work. The strongest supportive anchor on the call and a genuine reason to spend — which makes the failure to convert it into a funding route more notable, not less.

unmet_demand.want: A way to start now at a price he can actually fund — he confirmed intent ('outside of kind of discussing the financial side, I would be interested') and was blocked only by the figure.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Only the $6,000 programme was offered, in two, three or six instalments. The $2,000/year or $200/month tier that this same rep presented to another prospect the previous day was never mentioned. He was sent a free video instead.

unmet_demand.want: The aerobic capacity to run 5-10 km with a friend, named as his single most concrete goal.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme was described as kettlebell conditioning that produces stamina as a by-product — 'it's burning more calories as a stamina thing' — with no running programming, no progression to a distance target, and no acknowledgement that he currently runs twice a week. Whether the offer produces a 10 km runner was never addressed.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of a right shoulder with a six-to-eight-year acromioclavicular separation history and a recurring elbow problem, so that joints stop capping his effort.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Promised in general terms — Trevor 'is going to really find out... your right shoulder, everything around that' and mobility work will 'reverse' the accumulated inconsistencies — with no mechanism described, no clinician question, and no acknowledgement that overhead ballistic loading is the specific movement class most exposed to an AC injury.

unmet_demand.want: Someone external to stop him changing his own programme — 'if I had some outside source to say, no, no, stop changing things, you know, you're doing this, we're seeing this through for this long.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Genuinely served by the offer, and the rep did describe check-ins and coach contact. Recorded because it is the buying reason and it went unnamed at the close: the value was never restated in the prospect's own terms at the moment the price landed.
